people.name: Antoninus Pius
people.fullName: Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius (Titus Aurelius Fulvus Boionius Arrius Antoninus)
people.summary: Wealthy senator of Gallic (Nemausus) origin adopted by Hadrian in 138 on condition he adopt Marcus and Lucius. His 23-year reign, spent entirely in Italy, was the most peaceful of the Principate, marked by the Antonine Wall, legal humanity and a full treasury.
people.detail: Marcus's portrait of him (Meditations 1.16) is the fullest sketch of an ideal ruler from someone who knew him intimately: patient, thorough, frugal, courteous, indifferent to flattery. The lack of narrative sources leaves his reign almost without events, which Gibbon took as the mark of a happy age.

people.name: Faustina the Elder
people.summary: Wife of Antoninus Pius and aunt of Marcus Aurelius, deified after her death in 140 and commemorated by the Temple of Antoninus and Faustina and the girls' charity of the puellae Faustinianae.

people.name: Marcus Aurelius
people.fullName: Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus (born Marcus Annius Verus)
people.summary: Philosopher-emperor, adopted at Hadrian's behest, who shared power with Lucius Verus, faced the Parthian war, the Antonine Plague, the Marcomannic Wars and the revolt of Avidius Cassius, and spent most of his last decade on the Danube writing the Meditations. He broke with adoption by making his son Commodus co-emperor.
people.detail: Educated by Fronto in rhetoric and by Junius Rusticus in Stoicism; his correspondence with Fronto survives in a palimpsest. His reign saw Christian martyrdoms (Justin, Lyon) under the existing legal framework. His equestrian statue on the Capitol and his column in the Campus Martius survive. Dio judged his death the end of a golden age.
people.death: illness, possibly plague, at Vindobona or Sirmium, 17 March 180

people.name: Lucius Verus
people.fullName: Imperator Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus (born Lucius Ceionius Commodus)
people.summary: Son of Lucius Aelius Caesar, co-emperor with Marcus from 161, nominal commander of the victorious Parthian war (162-166) waged by his generals; he married Marcus's daughter Lucilla and died of a stroke while returning from the Danube.

people.name: Faustina the Younger
people.summary: Daughter of Antoninus Pius, wife of Marcus Aurelius and mother of at least thirteen children, including Commodus and Lucilla; she accompanied Marcus on campaign (hailed 'mother of the camp') and died at Halala, suspected by hostile sources of encouraging Avidius Cassius.
people.death: natural causes at Halala, Cappadocia, winter 175/176

people.name: Lucilla
people.summary: Daughter of Marcus Aurelius, married to Lucius Verus at Ephesus in 164 and then to Tiberius Claudius Pompeianus; resentful of Commodus's wife's precedence, she organised the failed assassination attempt of 182 and was exiled and killed.

people.name: Commodus
people.fullName: Imperator Caesar Lucius Aelius Aurelius Commodus Augustus
people.summary: Son of Marcus Aurelius, the first emperor 'born in the purple' to a reigning emperor. He ended the Marcomannic Wars by treaty, left government to favourites (Perennis, Cleander), survived conspiracies, increasingly identified himself with Hercules and fought in the arena, and was strangled on the last night of 192.
people.detail: Dio, a senator under him, and Herodian give lurid portraits; the Historia Augusta is worse. Modern historians (Hekster) read his Hercules persona as a deliberate appeal to the plebs and army over the Senate's head. His death ended the Antonine dynasty and began the civil wars of 193.
people.death: strangled in his bath by the wrestler Narcissus, 31 December 192

people.name: Avidius Cassius
people.summary: Syrian-born general, son of an equestrian secretary of Hadrian, famed for brutal discipline, who sacked Seleucia and Ctesiphon (165), suppressed the Bucoli (172) and held a supreme command over the East until his proclamation as emperor in 175 on a false rumour of Marcus's death.
people.death: murdered by a centurion after three months as usurper, July 175

people.name: Statius Priscus
people.summary: Experienced general who rose from the equestrian militia, transferred from Britain to Cappadocia, and recaptured and destroyed Artaxata in 163.

people.name: Sedatius Severianus
people.summary: Gallic-born governor of Cappadocia who, encouraged by the oracle of Alexander of Abonuteichos, marched into Armenia and lost his army and his life at Elegeia in 161.

people.name: Martius Verus
people.summary: General of the Parthian war who later as governor of Cappadocia stayed loyal to Marcus during Cassius's revolt and burned the rebel's correspondence; consul for the second time in 179.

people.name: Vologases IV
people.summary: Arsacid king who invaded Armenia and Syria in 161 and lost Seleucia, Ctesiphon and northern Mesopotamia to the generals of Lucius Verus.

people.name: Lollius Urbicus
people.summary: Berber-born senator from Tiddis in Numidia who served in the Bar Kokhba war, reconquered southern Scotland and built the Antonine Wall, and later presided as city prefect over the trial in Apuleius's circle.

people.name: Aelius Aristides
people.summary: Greek orator of the Second Sophistic from Mysia, author of the panegyric To Rome, the Sacred Tales recording his dream-cures by Asclepius, and a lament for Eleusis sacked by the Costoboci.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.summary: Alexandrian astronomer, geographer and mathematician, author of the Almagest, Geography, Tetrabiblos and Harmonics, whose models dominated science for fourteen centuries.

people.name: Justin Martyr
people.summary: Greek-speaking philosopher from Samaria who converted to Christianity, taught in Rome, wrote two Apologies and the Dialogue with Trypho, and was beheaded under the city prefect Junius Rusticus.

people.name: Galen

roles.t: Physician to Marcus Aurelius and Commodus

people.summary: Physician of Pergamon, trained on gladiators, who became court doctor to Marcus Aurelius and Commodus; his vast output (about a sixth of all surviving Greek literature before 350) includes the key descriptions of the Antonine Plague and, in De indolentia, the loss of his library in the fire of 192.

people.name: Gaius
people.summary: Mysterious jurist known only by his praenomen, perhaps teaching in the East, author of the Institutes (c. 161), the one classical Roman legal work to survive almost complete, rediscovered in Verona in 1816.

people.name: Herodes Atticus
people.fullName: Lucius Vibullius Hipparchus Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes
people.summary: Fabulously rich Athenian sophist, tutor of Marcus Aurelius and consul in 143, benefactor of the Odeion in Athens, the Panathenaic stadium and the nymphaeum at Olympia; he chose the holders of Marcus's Athenian chairs.

people.name: Blandina
people.summary: Slave woman martyred at Lyon in 177, whose endurance under days of torture is the centre of the letter of the churches of Vienne and Lyon.
people.death: killed in the amphitheatre at Lyon, 177

people.name: Ballomar
people.summary: King of the Marcomanni who led the eleven-tribe embassy to the governor of Pannonia in 166/167 and is probably the leader of the invasion of Italy in 170.

people.name: Marcus Claudius Fronto

roles.t: Governor of the three Dacias and Upper Moesia

people.summary: Veteran of the Parthian war who governed the combined Dacian and Moesian command and died fighting Germans and Iazyges in 170; a statue in Trajan's Forum honoured him (ILS 1098). Not to be confused with the orator Fronto.

people.name: Claudius Pompeianus

roles.t: Senior commander in the Marcomannic Wars

people.summary: Syrian-born general from Antioch, Marcus's chief commander and son-in-law (husband of Lucilla), who drove the invaders from Italy in 170, advanced Pertinax, opposed Commodus's peace and twice refused the throne.

people.name: Valerius Maximianus
people.summary: Equestrian officer from Poetovio, adlected into the Senate, whose career inscription from Diana Veteranorum records that he killed Valao, king of the Naristi, with his own hand; he commanded the winter camp at Laugaricio.

people.name: Perennis
people.summary: Praetorian prefect who effectively ran the government for Commodus after 182, until a delegation of the British army accused him of conspiring to make his son emperor.
people.death: handed over to the soldiers and killed, 185

people.name: Cleander
people.summary: Phrygian former slave who rose to dominate Commodus's court, selling magistracies (25 consuls in one year), until a grain riot forced Commodus to sacrifice him.

people.name: Ulpius Marcellus
people.summary: Austere, sleepless governor of Britain sent by Commodus to repel the northern invasion of the early 180s; Dio describes his relentless discipline.

people.name: Maternus
people.summary: Deserter who led bands of soldiers and brigands through Gaul and Spain and plotted to kill Commodus at the Hilaria; betrayed and beheaded (Herodian).

people.name: Marcia
people.summary: Freedwoman and mistress of Commodus, said to favour Christians (she secured the release of confessors from the Sardinian mines), who organised his murder with Laetus and Eclectus; she was executed by Didius Julianus.
